# ces-revisions — roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md, specs/ces-revisions-research-chatgpt.md, specs/ces-revisions-research-claude.md, specs/ces-revisions-research-gemini.md.
Choices made:
- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`), managed with uv.
- Stack named in specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md (Part C, implementation notes): NumPyro, Dynamax, Blackjax if warranted, ArviZ, Polars.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | How the size of the one-month revision moves with the number of collection days before first release | A | 1 | Release calendar and monthly vintages: a day or two to assemble, from public release dates and archived releases. Fit time on about 40 years of monthly vintages: measured by Stage 1 |
| O3 | How much of the one- and two-month revisions comes from late sample reports, and how much from seasonal-factor revision | A | 2 | Needs both NSA and SA vintages. Fit cost: unknown until its stage runs on real data |
| O2 | How the size of the two-month revision moves with the first-closing collection rate | A | 3 | Collection-rate series from published tables. The vintages are shared with O1. Fit cost: unknown until its stage runs |
| O6 | How revision size moves with CES sample size and sample attrition | B | 1 | Sample size and attrition must be hand-built from archived releases and technical notes. Cost: measured by Stage 2 |
| O4 | How revision size moves with real BLS appropriations, continuing resolutions and shutdowns | B | 2 | Several days to hand-build from budget justifications |
| O5 | How revision size moves with BLS staffing counts | B | 3 | Several days to hand-build from FedScope and budget justifications |

Tracks: A — collection interval and revision size (research). B — budget, staffing and attrition (research). B is split from A for two reasons:
- A rests on sharp month-to-month calendar variation that public release dates give directly.
- B's covariates move slowly, trend together and must be hand-built, and its answer does not change A's model.

Track ranking: A, then B.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Collection days and one-month revision size
      Objective: Estimate how the scale of the one-month revision moves with collection days before first release, on real vintages.
      Outcomes: O1
      Track: A
      Consumes: nothing (the package is a scaffold)
      Produces: the monthly vintage panel and release calendar on real data; specs/ces-revisions-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: The findings file reports the estimated relationship between collection days and one-month revision scale over the real vintage history. It also records the measured cost of the real run: assembly time, data volume and fit wall time.
      Leaves out: release provenance manifest (Ranked list A, item 3); full validation suite (Ranked list A, item 4); supersector partial pooling (Ranked list A, item 5)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Sample size, attrition and revision size
      Objective: Estimate how revision scale moves with CES sample size and sample attrition, on real data.
      Outcomes: O6
      Track: B
      Consumes: Stage 1's monthly vintage panel
      Produces: the hand-built sample-size and attrition series; specs/ces-revisions-stage-2-findings.md
      Exit: The findings file reports the estimated relationship between sample size, attrition and revision scale, including what the slow-moving variation can and cannot identify. It also records the measured cost of the real run: hand-build time and fit wall time.
      Leaves out: release provenance manifest (Ranked list A, item 3); full validation suite (Ranked list B, item 3); supersector partial pooling (Ranked list B, item 4)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Ranked list — Track A

Items 1–2 are in your partner's order. Items 3–5 are later qualities, placed after the ranked outcomes, to be ranked at resume.

1. O3 — needs NSA and SA vintages; fit cost unknown until run

5. Supersector partial pooling of driver coefficients (picks up "supersector partial pooling" for Stage 1)
